parsed.explanation: The quoted sentence appears verbatim in the 'Current best' section and means what the objection takes it to mean: Part B is unproven. The write-up itself concedes the gap ('BUT such a signed sum is NOT always realizable by cancel/chain ops... Realizability gap'; 'Full proof... Part B open'). Checking the whole text, no all-n upper-bound argument exists anywhere: only the pigeonhole (which yields a small signed sum but, as the text itself notes with the {1,2} example, no XY realization via ≤ n cuts), the m ≤ n reduction, and a conjectural/empirical candidate ('min over subsets of greedy-chain seems ≤ T_n... Need to verify harder + prove'). Under the rubric, obligation (U) requires a written-out all-n mechanism; conjectures and 'to do' items earn no credit. The objection's witness is accurate, and without Part B the optimality half is missing, so the proof is incomplete.
